Sean, saw Clearspeed's 60M dollar Series D and the push to expand voice-based risk assessment across insurance.

Scaling that fast usually means more in-market carriers and insurers than your team can personally touch before the new reps ramp. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Clearspeed off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress around 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Sean, quick follow-up for Clearspeed.

Post-raise, board expectations on insurance pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble to recover.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your insurance segment needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.

Sean, last bit of proof for Clearspeed.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to 2.7M dollars in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Clearspeed's reply rate likely compares to other insurtech and risk software companies. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

Sean, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling insurance pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority right after the Series D, no problem at all. Timing is everything post-raise, and I know the fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your insurance motion? I'll tailor it to Clearspeed either way.
